audience.text: Developers who generate or modify PowerPoint presentations on a server or in a build pipeline and need to work directly inside the .pptx file format without external dependencies.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations, open existing ones from file or stream, save to file or stream, and save subsets of slides by index.
capabilities.title: Create and modify presentations

capabilities.text: Add 190 ShapeType auto shapes, picture frames, tables, and connectors bound to shapes via connection sites.
capabilities.title: Add and format shapes

capabilities.text: Set character formatting (bold, size, font, spacing, caps), paragraph formatting (alignment, indentation, bullets), and text frame properties.
capabilities.title: Format text and paragraphs

capabilities.text: Embed images from byte arrays, InputStreams, or IImage objects, and create tables with rows, columns, merged cells, and cell formatting.
capabilities.title: Add images and tables

capabilities.text: Add speaker notes slides per slide, create comment authors, add comments with position and timestamp, and support threaded comment replies.
capabilities.title: Manage notes and comments

capabilities.text: Apply solid, gradient, pattern, picture, and no-fill formats; configure line width, dash style, cap, join, and arrowheads; add shadow, glow, reflection, and 3-D effects.
capabilities.title: Apply fills, lines, and effects

limitations.text: Only three SaveFormat values (PPTX, POTX, PPSX) are supported; 22 other SaveFormat values raise UnsupportedOperationException.
Cloning a master slide via getMasters().addClone(...) does not persist to the saved package despite the collection reporting a size increase.
Generated presentations contain no lang= attribute in the package, so PowerPoint uses the authoring machine's default language instead of one declared in the file.
The library does not support charts, animations, transitions, themes, backgrounds, group shapes, hyperlinks, sections, SmartArt, OLE objects, or macro-enabled files.
Unknown parts such as presProps, viewProps, tableStyles, themes, and unused layouts are preserved byte-for-byte during round-tripping but are not modeled or editable.
Version 26.7.0 is not supported for security reasons and lacks XML hardening; users must build from source or use 26.8.0.

problems_solved.text: Enables server-side PowerPoint presentation generation and modification without requiring a local PowerPoint installation or native libraries.
Provides a pure Java, dependency-free solution for .pptx manipulation with zero runtime dependencies as confirmed by the CycloneDX SBOM.
Supports deterministic, reproducible builds with byte-identical outputs across builds and platforms.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Java is an MIT-licensed Java library that creates, reads, and edits PowerPoint .pptx presentations by building the Office Open XML package directly, with no PowerPoint installation, native code, or runtime dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of public symbols beyond those listed is not fully enumerated in the facts.
Whether the library supports reading or writing custom XML parts beyond carrying them through unchanged is not confirmed.
The behavior when opening malformed or non-standard .pptx files is not specified.
Whether the library supports embedded fonts or font substitution is not stated.
The scope of 'unknown parts' that are carried through unchanged is not fully defined beyond presProps, viewProps, tableStyles, themes, and unused layouts.

workflows.name: Create and save presentations
workflows.text: Developers instantiate a Presentation object, add shapes, text, tables, images, notes, and comments, then save to a file path or output stream in PPTX format.

workflows.name: Read and inspect presentations
workflows.text: Developers open existing .pptx files via path or input stream, iterate slides and shapes, extract text and formatting, and access notes and comments.

workflows.name: Stream-based processing
workflows.text: Developers use try-with-resources with InputStream and OutputStream to process presentations without writing intermediate files to disk.

workflows.name: Test-driven development
workflows.text: Developers run 3,638 tests including 232 conformance tests that unzip and assert on the produced .pptx package structure directly.
